sections.h2: What does the Greenup County Clerk do when a house is sold?
sections.html:
The Clerk records the deed and the mortgage that go with a sale, and that recording is what puts the new owner on the public record. The Greenup County Clerk's office describes its services as vehicle registration and titling, recordings, marriage licenses, notary bonds, elections and the sale of the delinquent tax bill. For a seller, the first and last of those matter most.

A deed is filed in the county where the land lies, so a house in Greenup, Flatwoods, Raceland, Russell, South Shore, Worthington or Wurtland is recorded here. Documents can go through an e-recording vendor or be brought to a counter. Ask the title company or closing attorney who is responsible for the recording and the transfer tax, then keep the recorded copy.

The Clerk also holds the tax bills that the sheriff passes along after April 15, and it runs the sale of those delinquent bills. Our Greenup County property tax guide covers that side in detail.

sections.h2: Where are the Greenup County Clerk's offices and when are they open?
sections.html:
The Clerk has three locations, and all are open Monday through Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The main office is in the Greenup County Courthouse, Room 208, at PO Box 686, Greenup, KY 41144, phone (606) 473-7394. The South Shore branch closes for lunch from noon to 1:00 p.m.

  • Main office, Greenup County Courthouse, Room 208: (606) 473-7394, fax (606) 473-5354.
  • Flatwoods branch, 2513 Reed Street, Suite 3: (606) 836-1944, fax (606) 836-1444.
  • South Shore branch, 69 Narco Drive: (606) 932-6564, fax (606) 932-3691.

Ask the office whether a branch can record your document or whether it must go to the main office. The Clerk is closed on weekends and posts holiday hours on its website.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed or mortgage in Greenup County?
sections.html:
A deed costs $50 for the first five pages plus $3 for each additional page, and the Clerk adds transfer tax on top. The Clerk's recording fee schedule lists a minimum for each document type, and the amount grows with page count.

Selected Greenup County Clerk recording fees (source: Greenup County Clerk, Records page)
DocumentMinimum fee
Deed, easement, power of attorney or plat$50
Affidavit of descent$50
Mortgage$80
Mortgage with assignment$126
Release of mortgage, full or partial$46
Deed of correction$46
Lis pendens notice$46
Judgment lien$46
Will$47

State tax liens are listed at $5, which is far cheaper than the $46 federal lien filing. If a document is not on the schedule, the Clerk charges $46 for a filing with no specific statutory fee. Ask the office for the fee on your exact document before you mail a check, because the schedule gives minimums.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Greenup County sale?
sections.html:
The Clerk's FAQ puts the tax at $1.00 for each $1,000.00 paid for the property. On a sale at Greenup County's Census median value of $134,000, that works out to $134. A $200,000 sale would carry $200.

The tax is collected when the deed is recorded, and the amount rests on the price stated for the property, so the closing statement and the deed should agree. Your closing agent can tell you who pays it under your contract. If a deed transfers a property for no money, such as a gift between family members, ask the Clerk's office what tax and what wording on the deed apply.

Add the recording fee to the transfer tax to estimate the Clerk's total. On a $134,000 sale the deed fee and tax together come to $184 before any extra pages.

sections.h2: Can I record or search Greenup County land records online?
sections.html:
Yes. The Clerk lists five e-recording vendors: Indecomm, Hopdox, CSC, Simplifile and ePN, which let a closing agent submit documents without a trip to the courthouse. Individuals can search records through eCCLIX, an online version of the County Clerk Indexing system used by a large share of Kentucky clerks.

  • Private citizens who search for personal reasons can use Greenup County records at no charge, up to five searches a day.
  • Commercial users, such as title searchers and surveyors, pay a subscription and can add other counties.
  • eCCLIX lets users view or print documents filed by more than 85 Kentucky clerk offices.

sections.h2: How can I get alerts about deed or mortgage fraud in Greenup County?
sections.html:
Register for DOCALERT, a free service the Clerk offers through Software Management, LLC. You supply your name and an email address, and the system sends a message whenever a mortgage or deed in your name or your business name is recorded in Greenup County.

The alert is useful to anyone who owns a house they do not live in: a landlord, an heir holding a parent's home, or an owner whose property is vacant while it is for sale. If a deed or mortgage you did not sign is recorded, the message gives you a reason to contact the Clerk and an attorney.

sections.h2: What does the Clerk do about delinquent property taxes?
sections.html:
The Clerk receives every unpaid real property bill from the sheriff on April 15 and records a lien against each parcel, and later sells the bills that remain unpaid. The Clerk's delinquent taxes page links to third-party purchaser information, an application and the state's delinquent tax listing.

Under the Department of Revenue's process, the sale falls 90 to 135 days after the transfer, notices go out from the county attorney, and the bills are advertised 30 to 45 days before the sale. Interest runs at 1 percent per month, and commissions and a lien recording and release fee are added. Payments made before the sale go through the Clerk's office. After the sale, a third-party purchaser holds the lien and you pay that buyer.

Anyone selling a house with a bill at the Clerk should get a payoff in writing and have the closing agent pay it from the proceeds, so the lien release is recorded with the deed.

faqs.q: How much does the Greenup County Clerk charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: $50 for the first five pages and $3 for each added page, plus transfer tax of $1.00 per $1,000 paid for the property. Ask the office for the total on your specific document.

faqs.q: What are the Greenup County Clerk's hours?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. at the courthouse, Flatwoods and South Shore offices. The South Shore branch closes from noon to 1:00 p.m. for lunch.

faqs.q: Where do I call the Greenup County Clerk?
faqs.a: The main office number is (606) 473-7394. Flatwoods is (606) 836-1944 and South Shore is (606) 932-6564.

faqs.q: Is searching Greenup County land records free?
faqs.a: For residents searching for personal reasons, yes, up to five searches a day through eCCLIX. Businesses that research records pay a subscription.
